newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia considering bank proposals for telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Russia considering bank proposals for telecoms.

text.p: Russia's privatisation ministry, the State Property Committee, is considering proposals from the Most Bank and Alfa Bank groups to become financial advisers for the sale of state telecoms holding company AO Svyazinvest, committee Chairman Alfred Kokh said on Tuesday.
"We are considering their proposals," he told Reuters.
He declined to say whether other institutions were under consideration.
Earlier the committee said it had dropped London investment bank N.M. Rothschild as consultant for the sale of Svyazinvest.

The Financial Times said the Most and Alfa groups, which it said were close to President Boris Yeltsin, had replaced Rothschild as part of a backlash against foreign investment, and would themselves be major investors in the privatisation.
Rothschild, together with the Russian Privatisation Centre, had been working with the authorities on the sale of a 25 percent stake in Svyazinvest to a strategic investor.
Last year Italian telecom holding company Stet SpA won a tender for the Svyazinvest stake but the deal fell through before completion.

Earlier this month the Russian authorities decided to transfer the government's 38 percent stake in national telephone company Rostelekom to Svyazinvest. The stake amounts to 51 percent of the voting shares in Rostelekom.
The stake in the new Svyazinvest will not be sold to a single strategic investor, but in parts to portfolio investors, starting early next year, the property committee said.
